title: Accept --root before the subcommand
lead:
`adj --root DIR list` exits 2 with "unknown command"; only `adj list --root DIR`
works. Agents and the owner trip on it.
findings_note: S17 dogfood friction (7), note on S20; C165

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: S17 dogfood friction item 7. The release (C165) fixes it before 0.1.0.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/cli/cli.go`: before dispatch, take a leading `--root DIR` / `--root=DIR` and pass it to the command as if it followed the subcommand.
- `internal/cli/cli_test.go`: tests.
- `README.md`, `internal/commands/ai.md` (if they say flags must follow the command).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `TestRootBeforeCommand`: `adj --root DIR list`, `adj --root=DIR inbox --json` and `adj --root DIR ask ...` behave exactly like the same flags after the command (same stdout, stderr and exit code) against a temp store.
- `TestRootTwice`: `--root` both before and after the command is a usage error (exit 2) naming both, unless the implementer records another rule in the catalog.
- `TestUnknownLeadingFlag`: any other flag before the command still exits 2 with usage.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
- Only `--root` (and the existing `--help`/`-h`) is accepted before the command. Do not add other global flags here; `--version` is S31's.
- The exact rule for `--root` given twice is the implementer's call, recorded per C32.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - `. scripts/env.sh && go test ./... && go vet ./... && test -z "$(gofmt -l cmd internal)"` passes.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body:

the owner asks; no AI attribution.
